body_md:
Assume that $F_\varepsilon(\rho_\varepsilon)\leq C$. Then functions $\rho_\varepsilon(\xi)$ converge strongly in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, up to a subsequence, to a function $\rho_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and such that $F_0(\rho_0)<\infty$.
	\label{Th32}

title: Theorem
body_md: Under conditions \eqref{trohy_umov} there exists a bounded continuous solution $v$ of problem \eqref{nu_nu4} and there is a constant $C_v$ such that $|v(\xi)-C_v|\xi^n\to 0$ as $\xi\to \infty$, $\forall n>0$. Moreover, if $f(\xi)\geq 0$ then $v(\xi)\geq 0$,  $C_v\geq 0$ (and $C_v> 0$ unless $f\equiv 0$).

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem73} It is straightforward to see that the function $\varphi(\xi):=\tilde\varphi(\xi)-q_0$ is a continuous solution of \eqref{eq_varphi} decaying faster than any negative power of $\xi$, 
 	as $\xi\to\infty$. Then, since the function $\phi_1$ in the definition \eqref{phi_ve_last} of $\phi_\varepsilon$ is given by $\phi_1(\xi)=\phi_0^\prime(0)\varphi(\xi)$, we have  	
$$
 	\phi_\varepsilon(\varepsilon^{1/3} \xi)=\varepsilon^{1/3} \phi_0^\prime(0)(\xi+\tilde\phi(\xi))+O(\varepsilon^{2/3})\geq c \varepsilon^{1/3}, \quad c>0,
$$
when $0\leq \xi \leq C$.
